content:
SANTA TERESA, N.M. (KVIA) -- A loud boom noise heard in the Santa Teresa area may have come from a fire at an abandoned country club, according to Dona Ana County Sheriff Kim Stewart.

Ariana Parra, a Dona Ana County spokesperson, said officials haven't confirmed whether the reported booms are connected to the fire. She said reports of the booms were made at 11:30 Tuesday night. The fire wasn't reported until just before 5 a.m. on Wednesday.

"I can't say 100% whether there is the connection with the loud booms last night," Parra said. "The loud booms were reported and nothing was found at that point in time, and then 4:55 this morning is what time the fire was reported."

Parra added that she's not ruling out the possibility that the fire and booms are unrelated. Investigators are looking into both incidents.

The Sunland Park Fire Department and Doña Ana Fire Rescue responded to a large fire were called out to the fire on Feathermoon Drive. Officials said it was near the Santa Teresa Golf Course.

The building, formerly known as the Santa Teresa Country Club, has been permanently closed for several years.

It took about 45 minutes to contain, officials said. Parra said nobody was in the building at the time of the fire.

Now, the Doña Ana Fire Marshal's office is investigating the fire.

@SunlandParkFire and Doña Ana Fire Rescue responded to a working structure fire on Feathermoon Dr. Crews arrived to a fully involved structure at the Santa Teresa Country Club. Fire under investigation by Doña Ana Fire Marshal's office Time out: 4:55 am https://t.co/veibky2reH

— Sunland Park Fire (@SunlandParkFire) November 11, 2026

Neighboring residents told ABC-7 that the boom was so loud, it sounded like gunshots or a plane crash.

Denise Lara said she heard the noise around 11 p.m. Tuesday. She said it shook her house and windows.

ABC-7 reached out to Oracle to ask if the reported boom sounds were tied to the Project Jupiter data center in the area. Oracle and Parra said the incident didn't happen at the Project Jupiter campus.

At the scene of the fire, ABC-7 saw the Dona Ana County bomb squad. Parra said the bomb squad was there out of an abundance of caution, and there isn't a threat to the public.
